definitions.explanation: A building with only one floor, as opposed to a multi-story structure. Common in residential architecture, especially in suburban and rural Japan.

examples.japanese: {平屋|ひらや}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}んでいる→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
examples.english: I live in a one-story house.
I want to live in a one-story house in my old age.

examples.japanese: ⟦{階段|かいだん}→階段：00782_kaidan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{平屋|ひらや}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}→高齢者：15649_koureisha⟧⟦にとって→にとって：06803_nitotte⟧⟦{暮|く}らし→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧やすい。
examples.english: Since there are no stairs, a one-story house is easy for elderly people to live in.

notes:
USAGE:
Refers specifically to buildings with only one floor. In recent years, single-story houses have gained renewed popularity in Japan due to their accessibility for aging residents and their simpler construction.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}て (single-story construction)
- {平屋|ひらや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{住宅|じゅうたく}→住宅：03280_juutaku⟧ (single-story residence)
- {平屋|ひらや}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{建|た}て{替|か}える→建て替える：10541_tatekaeru⟧ (to rebuild as a one-story house)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{二階建|にかいだ}て→二階建て：03001_nikaidate⟧: two-story building
- ⟦{一戸建|いっこだ}て→一戸建て：19687_ikkodate⟧: detached house (may have multiple floors)
